replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
I have looked all over, pretty extensively; there is no good tool for doing this right now. 

The best workflow for accomplishing this is to use a video generator to make a character, attempt to manually capture frames from the video generator when/if it decides to spin a character around, manually stitch those captured frames into a sprite sheet and then work from there. 

The results are almost universally awful, and because of the way the only good video generators currently work, the type of images you get mean that your sprites look like... well, basically like the old Mortal Kombat games, at best, except also VERY AI instead of live action. 

Realistically, right now, there is no good way of making a rotating 2D sprite. If you want a rotating character, you have to burn credits letting Astra make stuff in Blender.
